cross_component_finding: This page's statement of the wildcard/requireAccess() asymmetry is materially more precise than round 3's access-control-concepts.json version ('Users granted access using the all channels wildcard do not inherit requireAccess() rights to any specific channel'): this page spells out the actual mechanism - requireAccess() 'will only recognize grants made explicitly using a channel name (not by a wildcard)' - and gives a concrete failing call, requireAccess('anychannelname'), rather than describing the behavior only in the abstract. Per the round's instruction to extract the fuller/authoritative version when a per-command page adds detail beyond the conceptual page's passing mention, this record uses this page's own quote as the evidence for the doesNotSatisfy relation rather than round 3's. Also notable: Example 2 on this page shows requireAccess(oldDoc.channels) - checking access against the PREVIOUS revision's channel list rather than the current one - a pattern with no equivalent shown for requireRole()/requireUser() in this batch's material, though nothing states it is unique to requireAccess().
